profile.name: Dongnae yaryu
profile.tagline: Traditional Korean masked drama play featuring satire and outdoor performance.
profile.insight: Performed on the 15th of the Lunar New Year, this masked drama features masks made from gourds and leather covered in mulberry paper.
profile.profile: Dongnae yaryu is a traditional masked drama play in Korea performed for over 120 years in Oncheon-dong, Dongnae-gu. It has been named by the government of Korea as one of the Important Intangible Cultural Properties of Korea. The performance features satire and criticism toward commoners and noblemen, traditionally staged outdoors in a field.
profile.profile_long: Dongnae yaryu is a traditional masked drama play in Korea, rooted in the Gyeongsangnam-do province where outdoor theatrical traditions known as yaryu developed. The performance has a history spanning over 120 years in Oncheon-dong, Dongnae-gu, and was historically maintained by a professional theatre troupe called Ohgwangdae. Although its performance tradition was suspended in 1937, it was successfully reorganized in 1950 and subsequently recognized as one of the Important Intangible Cultural Properties of Korea. The event traditionally takes place on the night of the 15th day of the New Year according to the lunar calendar, originally serving as a prayer for farming prosperity and peace, though today it is performed more for celebration and entertainment. The festivities begin with a music group collecting donations from wealthy households at the start of the new year. On the festival day, townspeople gather at bridges such as Busan Bridge and Buma Bridge for a vibrant costume parade leading to the performance site. The parade is led by the character 'Nongjang', followed by other characters and musical bands. Upon arrival at the site, participants color their faces with Chinese ink or don elaborate masks made from gourds or leather, covered with handmade traditional mulberry paper and painted in vivid colors. The core contents of the drama center on biting satire and social criticism directed at both commoners and noblemen. While the specific choreography and dance steps are not documented in available texts, the performance relies on communal participation, masking, and theatrical parade traditions. The tradition connects deeply to the broader heritage of Korean talchum masked dances, preserving local cultural expressions through community organization and festive rituals.

sections.origins_and_history: Dongnae yaryu has been performed for over 120 years in Oncheon-dong, Dongnae-gu. The tradition was long maintained by Ohgwangdae, a professional theatre troupe. The celebration was suspended in 1937 and later reorganized in 1950, earning designation as an Important Intangible Cultural Property of Korea.
sections.how_it_is_danced: Technique not described in sources. The dance takes place outdoors in a field following a costume parade led by the character 'Nongjang', followed by other characters and bands. Participants color their faces with Chinese ink or put on masks to dance together.
sections.music_and_instruments: At the beginning of the new year, a music group is organized by townspeople to visit houses and collect money. On the festival day, bands follow the costume parade to the performance site. Specific instrument names are not detailed in the sources.
sections.costume_and_setting: The performance is set outdoors in a field. Participants gather at bridges for a costume parade. Masks are typically made from gourds or leather, covered with traditional Korean paper handmade from mulberry trees, and colored with paint.
sections.occasions_and_meaning: Performed on the night of the 15th day of the New Year according to the lunar calendar. It is traditionally a prayer for the prosperity of farming and for peace, though today it is performed more for fun. Its main contents are satire and criticism towards commoners and noblemen.
sections.notable_figures: The character 'Nongjang' leads the parade. The Ohgwangdae professional theatre troupe historically maintained the tradition.
sections.regional_variants: Yaryu refers to a drama performed outdoors in a field, especially in Gyeongsangnam-do province. A related variant named by the government is Suyeong Yaryu.
sections.lineage: Belongs to the broader category of talchum, traditional Korean masked drama plays.
